description:
Would this rule have made money? Replays recorded Kalshi quotes, second by second.

        Describe a rule for Kalshi's 15-minute crypto up/down contracts: which side
        to buy, when (minutes left), at what prices (cents), and optionally only when
        Sardine's history beats Kalshi's ask plus fee by `min_gap_cents` (side BEST
        picks whichever side has the larger gap). Sardine replays its per-second
        recordings of Kalshi's order book: one trade per window, a limit order at the
        ask landing after `latency_seconds`, filled only up to the size resting
        there, Kalshi's real fee, and Kalshi's official settlement.

        Returns profit per contract after fees with a 95% interval, win rate, fill
        behaviour, a zero-latency comparison (exposes stale-quote illusions), a
        first-half/second-half stability check, breakdowns by minutes left and
        price, and warnings. Results only; no raw data. Dates are UTC YYYY-MM-DD.
        Present results as what happened historically, never as a forecast.
name: backtest_rule
